sentences.text: Heyuannia was estimated to be 1.5 meters long and weigh twenty kilograms.
This dinosaur had a short, toothless skull with a steep snout.
It possessed very short arms and digits, with a reduced first digit.
Thousands of eggs, some likely laid by Heyuannia, were uncovered at the discovery site.
Fossils attributed to Heyuannia include one specimen that may contain reproductive organs.
Heyuannia was the first oviraptorid dinosaur discovered in China.
The holotype of Heyuannia huangi was found in the Dalangshan Formation near Huangsha, Guangdong.
Heyuannia yanshini was first described as the genus Ingenia yanshini by Rinchen Barsbold in 1981.
The arrangement of Heyuannia eggshells suggests a partially open nest and increased parental care.
Heyuannia was classified within the family Oviraptoridae by Lü in 2002.
The exact subfamily placement of Heyuannia is uncertain, with later analyses placing it in either Oviraptorinae or Ingeniinae.
Heyuannia lived from 83.6 to 66 million years ago during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages.
